rationale: The claim states that FAA's 2023 Zipline Exemption 19111B distinguishes operation-specific relief from authorization of the DAA system itself. The provided evidence, Exemption 19111B, explicitly supports this distinction by stating, 'The exemption does not authorize the system.' This statement, found within the FAA's response to DAA safety-standard comments, directly clarifies that while the exemption grants operational relief for Zipline to use a DAA system for specific Part 135 operations, it does not constitute a product-level authorization for the DAA system itself. No alternative interpretation, primary counterevidence, or scope limit within Exemption 19111B was found to defeat this explicit distinction. While a later amendment (Exemption 19111C) and separate DAA system approvals exist, these would pertain to the current status of DAA authorization or Zipline's overall authority, not retroactively negate the distinction made within Exemption 19111B at the time of its issuance.
evidence_locators: S-INTAKE-001-R2 (PDF printed page 10, FAA response to DAA safety-standard comments)
limitations: The full text of Exemption 19111C was not directly inspected for this review, though its existence was noted. Its content would primarily address the current status of Zipline's authority or DAA system authorization, not retroactively alter the distinction made within Exemption 19111B.
